prompt_text: Who was George Albert Smith? Birth Date: 4 April 1870
response_text:
**George Albert Smith (April 4 1870 – April 4 1951)** *8th President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter‑day Saints (LDS Church)* --- ### Early Life & Education | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Birth** | 4 April 1870, Salt Lake City, Utah Territory, United States | | **Parents** | George A. Smith (a prominent early LDS leader and grandson of church founder Joseph Smith) and Lucy Woodruff | | **Education** | • Attended public schools in Salt Lake City
• Graduated from the University of Utah (then the University of Deseret) with a degree in law (LL.B., 1895) | | **Marriage** | Married Lucy Woodruff (his cousin) on 23 June 1895; they had five children. | --- ### Professional & Civic Career | Period | Role | |--------|------| | **1895‑1900** | Practiced law in Salt Lake City; served as city attorney. | | **1900‑1903** | Elected to the Utah House of Representatives (Democrat). | | **1904‑1905** | Mayor of Salt Lake City; focused on public works, sanitation, and city‑wide improvements. | | **1905‑1910** | Served as a missionary for the LDS Church in the United Kingdom (including a stint as mission president). | | **1910‑1911** | Returned to Utah and resumed legal practice; also served as a judge of the Utah District Court. | --- ### Church Service | Year | Position | |------|----------| | **1903** | Ordained an **Apostle** of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles at age 33 (the youngest apostle in church history at that time). | | **1918‑1921** | Served as **President of the European Mission** (based in Great Britain). | | **1934‑1945** | Member of the **First Presidency** as **Second Counselor** to President Heber J. Grant. | | **1945‑1951** | Became the **8th President** of the LDS Church after the death of Heber J. Grant. | #### Highlights of His Presidency (1945‑1951) - **Post‑World‑War II Growth:** Oversaw rapid expansion of the church worldwide; membership grew from ~1.2 million to ~1.7 million. - **Welfare Program:** Strengthened the church’s welfare system, emphasizing self‑reliance, food production, and employment assistance for members. - **Missionary Work:** Increased the number of missionaries and opened new mission fields, especially in Europe, Latin America, and the Pacific. - **Temple Building:** Dedicated several new temples (e.g., the **Idaho Falls Temple** in 1945) and authorized plans for future ones. - **Education:** Supported the development of church‑run schools and the expansion of **Brigham Young University**. - **Public Relations:** Promoted a more outward‑looking image of the church, encouraging members to be “good citizens” and to engage positively with broader society. --- ### Personal Traits & Legacy - **Temperament:** Known for his calm, diplomatic demeanor and ability to mediate disputes—qualities that served him well both in politics and church leadership. - **Family:** His son, **George Albert Smith Jr.**, became a noted academic; his grandson, **George Albert Smith III**, served as a general authority in the LDS Church. - **Historical Significance:** Smith is remembered for guiding the LDS Church through the immediate post‑war era, laying groundwork for the global expansion that accelerated in the 1950s and beyond. --- ### Not to Be Confused With - **George Albert Smith (1860‑1951),** the English film pioneer and inventor, who was a contemporary but unrelated to the LDS leader. The film pioneer’s birth date was **1 January 1860**, not 4 April 1870. --- **In short:** George Albert Smith (1870‑1951) was a Utah lawyer, mayor, and long‑serving apostle who became the eighth president of the LDS Church. His tenure was marked by post‑World‑War II growth, welfare initiatives, and a focus on expanding missionary work and temple construction worldwide.
